quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch usually located?

options.text: Near the left handgrip
Near the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is located next to the right handgrip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Happen at night.
Are caused by bald tires.
Occur at speeds above 55 mph.
Involve inexperienced riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve inexperienced riders.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have ridden for less than six months. Most crashes happen during the day at low speeds.

questions.question: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle is similar to driving a car. However:

options.text: A motorcycle's visibility is more critical than that of a car.
A motorcycle's visibility is not as important as that of a car.
Passing should be done on the shoulder instead of on the main roadway.
It is critical to make eye contact with the other driver when riding a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle's visibility is more critical than that of a car.
questions.explanation: Visibility is more critical when riding a motorcycle. Motorcycles are small and can easily disappear into another vehicle's blind spot or be missed by other drivers.

questions.question: When being followed too closely by another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Move onto the shoulder.
Allow the other driver to pass you.
Exit the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the other driver to pass you.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle is tailgating you, safely change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make the problem worse by causing them to tailgate faster.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow all rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Read books about carrying passengers.
Practice riding on an empty road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the shoulder of a road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on an empty road.
questions.explanation: Practice on a quiet road before carrying a passenger in traffic. Your motorcycle will handle differently with the extra weight.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert riders about upcoming road hazards.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should travel:

options.text: More slowly than you would during the day under similar conditions.
At the speed you would travel during the day under similar conditions.
Faster than you would during the day under similar conditions.
On the shoulder of the road so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than you would during the day under similar conditions.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than you would during the day. It is harder to see hazards in the dark, and slower speeds help you avoid them.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, you should not:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Avoid making sudden moves.
Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow or stop, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oil, dirt, gravel, shade, and bridges—these areas are often slippery.

questions.question: If you are being chased by a dog, you should:

options.text: Kick it away.
Stop until the animal loses interest.
Swerve around the animal.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Dogs are attracted to motorcycles. If chased by a dog, slow down and approach it slowly. Then accelerate and ride away from it.

questions.question: What should an experienced rider do?

options.text: Change positions within their lane as conditions change.
Stay in one part of the lane at all times.
Weave within the lane to be more visible.
Travel only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change positions within their lane as conditions change.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle rider has three lane positions to choose from. Pick the safest position based on the road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding next to another rider?

options.text: It lets you use more of the road.
It limits your escape routes.
It lets you talk to the other rider.
It makes it easier for other cars to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: It limits your escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride next to another motorcycle. It reduces escape options if a hazard appears.

questions.question: How should you brake on a motorcycle?

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use the brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of proper lane positioning?

options.text: Avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Go faster.
Set up for turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go faster.
questions.explanation: Lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid blind spots, and prepare for turns. It does not help you go faster.

questions.question: How much braking power does the front brake provide?

options.text: 10 percent
25 percent
50 percent
75 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 75 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Where must a pass be completed?

options.text: A pass can be completed in a no passing zone.
You can go 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
The pass must start and finish in a passing zone.
The pass must be completed on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pass must start and finish in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: Only pass in safe, legal areas. Stay within the speed limit and follow all traffic laws.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle weaves over rain grooves or bridge gratings?

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Grip tight and speed up to get past the hazard.
Zigzag across the surface.
Ride on the shoulder instead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over grooves or gratings is usually not dangerous. Stay relaxed and ride straight at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Brake gradually.
Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slowly close the throttle to slow down, and move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: What is the best lane position?

options.text: Always the right portion of the lane.
Always the center portion of the lane.
Always the left portion of the lane.
It varies based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It varies based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as conditions change.

questions.question: Which action does NOT reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Stay alert.
Identify hazards and decide what to handle first.
Ride without a headlight.
Keep space around your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride without a headlight.
questions.explanation: Stay alert and identify hazards. Use your headlight to be more visible. Keep space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: When you must both brake and swerve to avoid a sudden hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then do the other.
Do both actions at the same time and press the brakes harder.
Do both actions at the same time, but focus mainly on swerving.
Do neither action.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then do the other.
questions.explanation: Your tires need good grip to swerve safely. Do not brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: What should you do to control your motorcycle well?

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up rather than to steer.
Press your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit so far back that you have to stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Press your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced in turns. Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Sit close enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: On short trips.
On long trips.
After riding for at least one hour.
After riding for more than 8 hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts riding.

questions.question: What should an effective face shield NOT do?

options.text: Be free of scratches.
Allow clear views to both sides.
Block air from passing through.
Fasten securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block air from passing through.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be free of scratches, block objects from hitting you, allow you to see clearly to both sides, fasten securely, and let air pass through. A face shield that blocks air can cause fogging, making it hard to see.

questions.question: Which statement about motorcycle crashes is true?

options.text: More than half happen at speeds over 35 mph.
More than half are caused by worn tires.
More than half happen in the dark.
More than half involve riders who are new to their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: More than half involve riders who are new to their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders who are new to their motorcycle.
